attributes.title: Level 1

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints:
❓ Where should the sprite’s [set sprite [ay (acceleration y)]] block be placed so that it pulls the Player sprite down? 

❓ Where should the sprite’s [set sprite [vy (velocity y)]] block be placed so that it moves the sprite upwards on the tilemap?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓What should happen when the A button is pressed?

❓What should happen after the A button is pressed?


Solution: 

💡The [set sprite ay (acceleration y)] and [set sprite vy (velocity y)] blocks should be swapped, so that the [set sprite ay (acceleration y)] block is in the [on start] container, and the [set sprite vy (velocity y)] is in the [on button pressed] container.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the A button doesn’t work as expected. 


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Player sprite begins the project on the ground and “jumps” when the A button is pressed.

subgroups.title: Debugging Acceleration and Velocity

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓Which value needs to be increased so “gravity” pulls the Player sprite down at a normal speed?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which value changes how quickly the Player sprite “floats” back to the ground?

❓ How might you change the ay value, so that the Player sprite falls back to the ground at a reasonable speed?


Solution: 

💡 The value in the [set sprite ay (acceleration y)] block should be changed to a value greater than 100, likely close to 500.
steps.instructions:
When the A button is pressed, the Player sprite “jumps” up on the screen, but “floats” down too slowly.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Player sprite’s acceleration acts as gravity, and lowers the Player sprite at a reasonable speed.

Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which block prevents the Player sprite from being able to jump from anywhere on the tilemap?


Solution: 

💡The direction in the <is sprite hitting wall> block should be changed from [left] to [bottom].

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Player sprite is able to jump over the Projectile obstacles on the screen!

validationItems.text: [bottom] is selected from the dropdown menu in the <is sprite hitting wall> block.
validationItems.failureText: Check the wall direction in the <is sprite hitting wall> block.

attributes.description: Welcome to Level 1 of Green Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about 2D platformer games and physics. In 2D platformers, we see the game as if looking from the side. We can use physics concepts, like velocity and acceleration, to make our sprites jump up onto platforms and avoid obstacles. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 1:

badges.title: Let’s Get Physics-cal!
badges.description: Use physics to control sprite movement in a platformer-style tilemap project.

badges.title: Hop, Skip, and a Jump
badges.description: Set a sprite’s y-velocity (vy).

badges.title: Defying Gravity
badges.description: Set a sprite’s y-acceleration (ay).

badges.title: Wallflower
badges.description: Check if a sprite is touching a tilemap wall before making something happen in a project.
